causal_change.factor: Boundary-selection policy for the representation-only normalization pass
causal_change.before: The first pass globally canonicalizes every major engine state domain, independent of which single algorithmic weakness the later strength pass will address.
causal_change.after: The first pass uses bounded task, metric, and capsule evidence to select one strength frontier and canonicalizes only its smallest complete transitive producer-consumer dependency closure, leaving semantics outside that closure unchanged before the same single forward strength transduction.
causal_change.why_causal: The normalization boundary controls both how much implementation information is disturbed and how much of the first call's reasoning is available to make the intended cross-component dependency explicit. Evidence-guided closure selection should retain the champion family's causal seam while avoiding unrelated rewrites. Routing the existing metrics and capsule into the first pass is only the operational means of choosing that one boundary; the two-call nonbranching family, representation-first ordering, and sole strength-bearing final transformation remain unchanged.

hypothesis.expected_effect: Compared with the champion structure on the same three anchors, the final engines should preserve the promoted family's coordinated dependency handling while suffering fewer incidental regressions and devoting more construction capacity to one consequential improvement. This predicts zero invalid candidate arms, a paired win majority, and candidate-median Elo strictly above the champion-structure median.
hypothesis.falsifier: After the complete three-pair matched batch, falsify the refinement unless all formal promotion conditions hold: three valid pairs, candidate wins strictly exceed losses, candidate-median Elo strictly exceeds incumbent-median Elo, and both arms have zero invalid results. Also treat an emitted first-pass artifact that globally rewrites unrelated domains or omits a producer or consumer required by the selected frontier as direct mechanistic evidence against the claimed boundary-selection effect.
hypothesis.behavioral_novelty: Before any strength edit, the loop can preserve unrelated engine subsystems while materializing an explicit executable seam around exactly the transitive state dependency implicated by bounded evidence. The final pass can then change that prepared closure once, rather than receiving a globally normalized engine whose unrelated semantics were rewritten regardless of relevance.
strengths: Preserves the supported two-pass, single-artifact executable-transduction lineage.
Concentrates normalization effort on every producer and consumer that the intended improvement actually couples.
Reduces semantic-drift and invalidity exposure by retaining unrelated anchor behavior.
Contains one artifact per pass and no replicated agents, candidate variants, sampling multiplicity, or best-of-N selection.
risks: Bounded evidence may point to a low-leverage frontier, causing the focused pass to spend capacity on the wrong subsystem.
An incorrectly computed dependency closure may omit a hidden consumer and make the final strength edit inconsistent.
Leaving unrelated representations intact may preserve an awkward interface that limits the prepared seam's usefulness.
The final transformer may exceed the prepared closure, erasing the expected reduction in incidental semantic change.

structure.name: Frontier-Scoped Single-Lineage Semantic Transduction
structure.information_flow: One nonbranching executable lineage: champion_engine plus bounded task evidence enters frontier_scoped_normalizer_engine; its sole complete engine enters frontier_strength_transducer_engine; that second call emits the sole final engine. The only refinement is how the first pass selects its normalization boundary.

calls.objective: Transform exactly one supplied anchor into exactly one complete runnable engine without introducing a playing-strength change. Use only the task, aggregate champion metrics, and bounded state capsule to identify one highest-leverage algorithmic frontier; do not inspect or encode benchmark cases. Trace that frontier to its smallest complete transitive closure of state producers, transitions, and consumers, then expose only that closure through explicit single-source executable seams. Preserve the search policy, evaluation intent, and implementation outside the closure except for adapters strictly required to keep the closure complete. Run bounded in-call equivalence, legality, UCI, make/unmake, hashing, repetition, and state-invariant probes relevant to the touched closure, repairing the same unfinished transduction in place. Do not tune engine hyperparameters, make a strength edit, generate alternatives, replicate candidates, or perform selection.

Consume the sole frontier-scoped canonical engine and emit exactly one complete production engine. Implement one coherent algorithmic strength improvement through the prepared dependency seam, updating every producer and consumer inside its closure while preserving behavior outside it. Use bounded legality, UCI, state-integrity, and tactical sanity checks and repair the same unfinished transformation in place if a check fails. Do not tune engine hyperparameters as the structural change, generate or compare alternatives, use replicated samples, invoke an external reviewer, attribute post-hoc source deltas, branch into competing semantics, or perform preserve-versus-rollback selection.
